title: Variant coordination timewarp caused overlapping routes; safe fallback runbook and follow-up
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a cross-region variant promotion a coordinator timing discrepancy resulted in a transient overlap where two route epochs were both active. The overlap caused duplicated routing decisions, capacity amplification for a small subset of customers, and an increase in tail latency for affected model variants. This ticket captures the incident timeline, immediate mitigations, and proposed long-term fixes plus owners and dates.
incident_timeline: 2025-03-14 09:05 UTC: Promotion job started to promote variant v2025-03-14-02 across regions as part of routine canary expansion.
2025-03-14 09:08 UTC: Region eu-west orchestrator applied epoch=42; region us-east lagged and reported epoch=41 but served traffic due to stale local routing cache.

2025-03-14 09:09-09:22 UTC: Monitoring alerted elevated 95th/99th latencies for v2025-03-14-02 and increased request-retries for some customers. Traffic telemetry showed ~0.6% mixed-serve across a subset of routes.
2025-03-14 09:23 UTC: Automated rollback gate did not trigger because promotion completed in primary region; manual rollback initiated by on-call.
2025-03-14 09:30 UTC: Manual rollback completed; traffic normalized by 09:36 UTC. Post-rollback verification run completed at 10:00 UTC.
2025-03-14 11:00 UTC: Triage call; assigned owners and began deeper investigation into coordinator commit fence and local cache TTLs.
root_causes: Leader transition latency in the cross-region coordinator caused a window where two orchestration epochs were accepted by different region actors.
Local route cache TTL was too long (30s) and caches were not invalidated when the coordinator advanced an epoch elsewhere, allowing stale routing to continue serving.
Promotion job used negative jitter in the rollout window which amplified inter-region timing differences under modest load.
No global monotonic fence enforced at proxy edge to guarantee single-epoch acceptance during promotions.
impact_summary: Approximately 0.6% of requests for the promoted variant experienced mixed routing (simultaneous eligibility in two variants) for ~14 minutes. This translated to higher tail latency and a small increase in error retries for a narrow set of customers using high-concurrency streaming paths. No data corruption or model state loss observed.
immediate_mitigations: Manual rollback of promotion in affected regions to previous stable epoch (completed at 09:36 UTC).
Shorten local route cache TTL from 30s to 5s as a hotfix to reduce overlap windows (rolled at 10:12 UTC).
Temporarily disable negative rollout jitter for cross-region promotions until sequencing fixes are in place.
Added a high-cardinality metric to detect mixed-serve (probe + verdict) and an alert threshold to catch future overlaps sooner.
long_term_action_items: (Owner: infra-team) Implement a global epoch fence enforced at the edge proxy so a request carries an accepted epoch and proxies reject requests outside the accepted window. Due: 2025-04-18.
(Owner: orchestration) Add a two-phase commit for cross-region promotions: prepare -> confirm -> commit with explicit ack from region leaders. Due: 2025-05-02.
(Owner: runtime) Introduce a promotion scheduler that computes safe promotion windows accounting for leader election latencies and region RTTs; remove negative jitter. Due: 2025-04-11.
(Owner: observability) Add synthetic mixed-serve canaries and a dashboard for variant overlap rate, with an automated runbook link. Due: 2025-03-28.
(Owner: SRE) Create an automated rollback play that can be invoked by PagerDuty with a single command and a preflight check for inconsistent epochs. Due: 2025-04-04.
(Owner: QA) Add integration tests that simulate asynchronous epoch application across three regions to catch timewarp scenarios. Due: 2025-05-16.
(Owner: product) Update rollout runbook to include explicit epoch fence checks and a promotion checklist for cross-region promotions. Due: 2025-03-31.
notes: This incident surfaced a class of race between local caches and global orchestration state. The fixes emphasize preventing overlap at the traffic-acceptance point rather than relying solely on faster propagation. We will schedule a cross-functional review on 2025-03-25 to align owners and finalize timelines.
